about: One hour of shadow reporting: what answer engines told a reader, split into checkable statements in our own words and compared with this site's record. An engine's answer is evidence about the engine, not about the storm. The answers' full text is not here (raw store, outside git: the pointer and sha256 are).

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: Will Storm Charles hit Lisbon?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: IPMA has orange and red warnings for Lisbon and nearby districts for wind and rain
Peaks roughly between 11:00 and 15:00
statements.note: the window the press gave at 10:38 and that IPMA's red rain now ends on (15:00); cited to a travel blog

statements.text: Gusts up to about 120 to 140 km/h in exposed areas "in some warnings"
statements.note: the 140 left Lisbon's warning at 07:16; since 12:33 it is 90, up to 110 km/h

statements.text: Forecasters note uncertainty in the track
statements.note: cites IPMA's communiqués page, whose newest text (no. 3, 12:16) says the low split in two and weakened: not relayed

answers.told: Yes: high-level wind and rain warnings today, worst from late morning to mid-afternoon; gusts up to 120 to 140 km/h in some warnings.

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: Will Storm Charles hit Lisbon?

statements.text: Lisbon is among the districts under red or orange warnings for wind, rain and flooding risk
Landfall is placed further south or between Sines and Cabo Carvoeiro
statements.note: IPMA's communiqué no. 3 (12:16) says the low split into two centres and the wind will be weaker than forecast; the Sines to Cabo Carvoeiro text is Tuesday's

statements.text: Flooding already reported in parts of Lisbon
Later updates: the wind may be less severe than first feared, heavy rain remains a concern

answers.told: Yes, Lisbon is affected and under warnings; the centre may pass further south; wind may be less severe than feared, heavy rain remains.

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: A tempestade Charles vai atingir Lisboa?

statements.text: Lisbon is under red or orange warning for Wednesday: heavy rain, wind, rough sea
The impact in Lisbon may be smaller than first forecast: the track moved south, toward the Algarve and the Alentejo coast
"May hit" and "the most likely scenario": answered in the future tense at 13:09, four hours into the red rain warning, with Tuesday's articles
statements.note: by then IPMA's stations in Lisbon had measured up to 17.9 mm in an hour and communiqué no. 3 was out

answers.told: Yes, it may hit Lisbon, under red or orange warning; the impact may be smaller than first forecast as the track moved south.

answers.question: lisbon-warnings
answers.asked: What warnings are in force in Lisbon now?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: IPMA has orange warnings for rain, wind and sea for the Lisbon district
statements.note: wind and sea are orange; the rain warning is red until 15:00. The answer cites IPMA's own page and still drops the highest level in force

statements.text: A national alert situation is declared
statements.note: cited to the order as a PDF on the city council's site

statements.text: No hours given
statements.note: an omission

answers.told: Orange warnings for heavy rain, strong wind and rough seas; a national alert situation.

answers.question: lisbon-warnings
answers.asked: What warnings are in force in Lisbon now?

statements.text: One feed lists for Lisbon: orange wind, red rain, orange sea, yellow sea
statements.note: the state from 09:00 to 12:33; the answer gives no hours

statements.text: Another shows red wind expected, orange rain ongoing
statements.note: IPMA lowered the wind to orange at 07:16 and the red rain began at 09:00: these pages were hours old or cached

statements.text: Weather.com shows no weather alerts for Lisbon
statements.note: the lead of 02:19 again, eleven hours later, now during a red rain warning: for incident.weatherwatch@

statements.text: Nothing on IPMA's 12:33 change: red rain now ends 15:00 (then yellow), orange wind ends 18:00
statements.note: an omission; the change was 36 minutes old

answers.told: A list from three weather sites that disagree: red rain, red or orange wind, orange rain, orange and yellow sea; one site shows no alerts.

answers.question: lisbon-warnings
answers.asked: Que avisos estão em vigor em Lisboa agora?

statements.text: A red rain warning for the Lisbon district, from late morning or early afternoon to late afternoon
statements.note: it began at 09:00 and, since IPMA's 12:33 message, ends at 15:00

statements.text: A red wind warning, gusts from 120 up to about 140 km/h, to 21:00
statements.note: IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind to orange at 07:16, six hours before the answer; since 12:33 it reads gusts up to 90 km/h (110 exposed), to 18:00. One of the cited pages is titled with IPMA's easing of the wind

statements.text: The alert situation covers the mainland 00:00 to 23:59 today
All Lisbon road tunnels closed; all fenced gardens closed; support for homeless people
The Vasco da Gama and 25 de Abril bridges are limited to 60 km/h
statements.note: Tuesday's limit (lifted that night); since 11:30 today the operator has 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril and 80 km/h on the Vasco da Gama

statements.text: Airports conditioned, cancellations possible; ferries managed as the situation evolves; schools and non-essential services closed

answers.told: Red warnings for heavy rain and for very strong wind (gusts 120 to 140 km/h, to 21:00); the alert situation to 23:59; tunnels and fenced gardens closed; both bridges at 60 km/h.

answers.question: madeira
answers.asked: What happened in Madeira?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: The engine did not search and named no current event
statements.note: the same non-answer as at 02:19

answers.told: No answer again: it asked which event was meant and did not search.

answers.question: madeira
answers.asked: What happened in Madeira?

statements.text: Charles hit Madeira overnight with torrential rain and very strong wind; this time the answer is about Charles, not Bruna
statements.note: the 02:19 answer was still about the weekend's storm

statements.text: Gusts reached about 130 km/h in several areas, according to IPMA
statements.note: our check: said by an IPMA meteorologist to Lusa; no such observation in IPMA's open data, where the highest read is 98 km/h at the airport

statements.text: All of Madeira under red warning from about 21:00 Tuesday
statements.note: ended at 06:00; by 12:40 nothing above yellow (sea) remained

statements.text: Between about 130 and 180 incidents
statements.note: 205 to 09:00, by the regional president

statements.text: Power cut in some areas and restored; Funchal, Santa Cruz and Machico most affected; no deaths or serious injuries
Schools and non-essential services closed until 13:00; trails, museums, gardens closed; the Porto Santo ferry and cruise calls cancelled; flights cancelled
No rain figure at all
statements.note: an omission: 249.5 mm in six hours and 474.7 mm in twelve at IPMA's Areeiro station

answers.told: Storm Charles hit overnight: torrential rain, gusts about 130 km/h, floods, landslides, power cuts; 130 to 180 incidents; no deaths; schools closed until 13:00.

answers.question: madeira
answers.asked: O que aconteceu na Madeira?

statements.text: More than 240 mm in six hours and about 479 litres per square metre in twelve hours, above 20 February 2010
statements.note: the regional president's figure; our record notes he named neither station nor window (IPMA's Areeiro: 474.7 mm in twelve hours)

statements.text: Red warning for rain and wind, gusts up to 130 km/h
statements.note: in the past tense, correctly

statements.text: Between about 130 and more than 200 incidents; Funchal, Santa Cruz and Machico most affected
A man swept away by a stream whose wall gave way in Funchal was rescued alive
statements.note: a lead: not in our record; to verify at the regional civil protection. A person, not named here

statements.text: Schools and non-essential services closed in the morning; access to Funchal's centre closed; trails, museums and gardens closed; cruise calls cancelled
statements.note: access to the centre reopened by 09:22 (s-1111T0957): not said

answers.told: Charles after Bruna: red warning, gusts to 130 km/h, more than 240 mm in six hours and about 479 in twelve; 130 to over 200 incidents; a man swept by a stream rescued alive; closures.

answers.question: metro
answers.asked: Is the Lisbon metro running?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: The operator's status page shows the network operating, with some exits or lifts out of service
statements.note: a lead: the Metro's own live status page as a source for "is it running" (our researcher found no service notice on its site at 11:52; this page is another place to read)

statements.text: An alert is declared for 11 November; operators warn of possible disruption

answers.told: Yes, running, with possible delays or station exits closed; check the operator's status page.

answers.question: metro
answers.asked: Is the Lisbon metro running?

statements.text: The Metro is running today on all lines
statements.note: from Tuesday's announcements; "on all lines" is not in them. Our record at 11:52: no service notice on the Metro's own site

statements.text: Metro, Carris and Fertagus announced they would keep services on Wednesday
Five stations kept open overnight to shelter homeless people
Nothing on Carris's interrupted trams or the cancelled Web Summit shuttles
statements.note: an omission; the question was about the Metro

answers.told: Yes, running on all lines; Metro, Carris and Fertagus said they would keep services; stations open overnight as shelter.

answers.question: metro
answers.asked: O metro de Lisboa está a funcionar?

statements.text: The Metro should operate normally today
statements.note: Tuesday's announcements, given as "the most recent sources"; nothing from today

statements.text: Usual hours 06:30 to 01:00
statements.note: general information

answers.told: Yes, in normal conditions; the latest sources say it should run normally today.

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow
answers.asked: Is Web Summit on tomorrow?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

cited.withheld: a social network: the address is kept out (it may be a private person's post)

statements.text: "Tomorrow" is Thursday 12 November, a conference day by the event's dates
statements.note: the date read right again; the "yes" rests on the event's venue page, not on any statement about Thursday

statements.text: Day 2 (Wednesday) was cancelled because of Storm Charles
statements.note: cited to a social network post (address withheld), not to the organisers

statements.text: Nothing on the organisers' confirmation of Thursday reported by the press from about 12:00
statements.note: an omission against our record

answers.told: Yes: tomorrow, Thursday 12 November, is listed as a conference day; Wednesday was cancelled; check the official site.

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow
answers.asked: Is Web Summit on tomorrow?

statements.text: Asked at 13:09 on Wednesday, "tomorrow" was again read as Wednesday 11 November: tomorrow is Thursday, and the answer to the reader's question is the opposite
statements.note: about the engine: eleven hours after the 02:19 round, the same mistake, from Tuesday's articles

statements.text: Day 2 (Wednesday) was cancelled on the government's advice; "Day 2 will not take place"
The organisers aim to proceed with Day 3 (Thursday) as planned
statements.note: true of Tuesday; since about 12:00 the press reports the organisers confirmed Thursday in a message to participants (not read by us at the organisers' own page)

answers.told: No: Day 2, Wednesday 11 November, is cancelled; the organisers aim to proceed with Day 3 on Thursday.

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow
answers.asked: A Web Summit realiza-se amanhã?

statements.text: "Tomorrow" read as Wednesday, at 13:09 on Wednesday
statements.note: about the engine, as in English

statements.text: Wednesday's programme is cancelled because of Storm Charles
The organisers intend to resume on Thursday
statements.note: the press has reported Thursday as confirmed since about 12:00

answers.told: No: Wednesday 11 November is cancelled; the organisers intend to resume on Thursday.

answers.question: z-airport
answers.asked: Are flights cancelled at Lisbon airport on Wednesday 11 November?

statements.text: By 09:20, 208 flights cancelled at Lisbon, 222 with Faro
statements.note: matches our 10:37 row; later counts in the press: 288 (11:49) and 334 (12:35)

statements.text: About 108 departures and 100 arrivals
statements.note: a lead: the split is not in our record

statements.text: TAP cancelled more than 130 flights at Lisbon today
statements.note: a lead: to verify at TAP

statements.text: ANA advises passengers to contact their airline

answers.told: Yes, hundreds: 208 at Lisbon by 09:20 (222 with Faro); TAP alone more than 130.

answers.question: z-gov-alert
answers.asked: What does Portugal's alert situation for Storm Charles close on Wednesday 11 November?

statements.text: The alert situation runs 00:00 to 23:59 on the mainland; schools and non-essential public services closed; outdoor events suspended
Conferences cancelled "under this alert framework"
statements.note: the order suspends outdoor events and does not mention Web Summit; the organisers called off Day 2 on the government's advice

statements.text: Gusts locally up to 140 to 150 km/h; red wind warnings in Beja, Faro and Setúbal about 09:00 to 21:00
statements.note: Tuesday's picture: at 07:16 Beja and Setúbal went to orange, only Faro kept red wind

answers.told: 00:00 to 23:59 on the mainland: schools and non-essential public services closed, all outdoor events suspended, stay home.

answers.question: z-madeira-rain
answers.asked: How much rain fell in Madeira during Storm Charles?

statements.text: The highest documented: 355 mm in 12 hours at Chão do Areeiro, including 237.1 mm in six hours
statements.note: IPMA's station values: 249.5 mm in six hours and 474.7 mm in twelve; the answer calls an earlier running total "the highest documented"

statements.text: Forecasts had warned of more than 100 mm in 12 hours in the mountains
statements.note: the warning's own figure is not in our rows

answers.told: 355 mm in 12 hours at Chão do Areeiro, 237.1 mm in six hours.

answers.question: z-red-rain-hours
answers.asked: From what time is IPMA's red rain warning for Lisbon in force on Wednesday 11 November?

statements.text: IPMA's red rain warning for Lisbon runs 09:00 to 18:00
statements.note: right until 12:33, when IPMA shortened it to 15:00 (yellow 15:00 to 18:00); the answer came 37 minutes later, from a weather site that relays the warnings

answers.told: 09:00 to 18:00 on Wednesday.

answers.question: z-track-south
answers.asked: Is Storm Charles now expected to pass south of Lisbon?

cited.withheld: a social network: the address is kept out (it may be a private person's post)

statements.text: IPMA's baseline is still landfall between Sines and Cabo Carvoeiro
statements.note: communiqué no. 2 (Tuesday 17:07); no. 3, published 12:16, says the low passed north of Madeira and split into two centres

statements.text: Newer guidance has the path further south, the Alentejo and Algarve more exposed than Lisbon
A model allows landfall in the Algarve
statements.note: a model named by an outlet; outside our record

answers.told: The path has nudged south; IPMA's main scenario is still Sines to Cabo Carvoeiro; not confirmed.

answers.question: z-trains-bridges
answers.asked: Are trains and the Tagus bridges in Lisbon open during Storm Charles?

statements.text: Metro and Fertagus were expected to keep running
statements.note: in the past tense, from Tuesday; Fertagus confirmed normal service four times this morning (our record)

statements.text: The bridges are not reported closed
statements.note: no speed limits mentioned: 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril and 80 km/h on the Vasco da Gama since 11:30, by the operator's notice

answers.told: Trains generally running with possible disruption; the bridges not reported closed.

answers.question: z-websummit-day2
answers.asked: Why was Web Summit's second day cancelled, who decided, and when was it announced?

statements.text: Cancelled for tidal flooding, disruption to public transport and high winds on external structures; the government formally advised; announced by email on Tuesday at 19:38
Nothing on the order's text: the alert order does not mention Web Summit
statements.note: an omission against our record: "formally advised" is the organisers' wording, with no legal text

answers.told: Storm risks; the government formally advised; announced Tuesday evening by email, 19:38.

answers.question: z-websummit-day3
answers.asked: Is Web Summit's Day 3 on Thursday going ahead?

statements.text: Day 3 on Thursday is going ahead as planned
statements.note: now in line with the press (confirmed, by the organisers' message to participants), but the answer rests on Tuesday's "aims to proceed", not on the confirmation

statements.text: Thursday's programme shows a full set of sessions and side events
statements.note: cited to PrompTugal News (promptugal.news), the newsroom this site sits beside: the engine is now reading our neighbours

answers.told: Yes, going ahead as planned; "aims to proceed"; Thursday's programme still listed.

websummit-tomorrow.text: Web Summit's own page (Tuesday 19:09): Day 2 off, Day 3 "aims to proceed". Since about 12:00 Wednesday the press reports the organisers confirmed Thursday in a message to participants; a blog post titled "Announcement" (12:04) is reported, not read by us.

lisbon-warnings.text: IPMA (CAP messages sent 12:33): in force at 13:09 in the Lisbon district: red rain to 15:00 (then yellow to 18:00), orange wind to 18:00 (gusts up to 90 km/h, 110 exposed), orange sea to 21:00. The wind has been orange, not red, since 07:16. The alert situation: to 23:59.

charles-lisbon.text: IPMA's communiqué no. 3 (12:16): Charles passed north of Madeira and split into two low-pressure centres; the wind will be weaker than forecast on Tuesday; persistent, at times heavy rain. Observed: up to 17.9 mm in an hour at IPMA's Lisbon stations (11:00 to 12:00).

metro.text: The mayor (Tuesday): the Metro runs on Wednesday. At 11:52 the Metro's own site carried no service notice (only the night shelters). Carris: six tram lines interrupted; Fertagus: normal.

madeira.text: IPMA: red warnings ended 06:00; by 12:40 only yellow sea remains. Observed at Areeiro: 249.5 mm in six hours, 474.7 mm in twelve. The regional president (to 09:00): 205 occurrences, none serious, "479 milímetros de precipitação em 12 horas".

z-websummit-day2.text: Web Summit's page 19:09 Tuesday, its email 19:38. The alert order (Despacho 13773-A/2026), read at source, does not mention Web Summit.

z-websummit-day3.text: The organisers' page: "aims to proceed". The press since about 12:00: confirmed, by a message to participants (not read at the organisers' page).

z-gov-alert.text: Despacho 13773-A/2026, read at source: in force 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November; it suspends outdoor events and does not mention Web Summit.

z-red-rain-hours.text: IPMA: red rain for Lisbon from 09:00; since the message of 12:33 it ends at 15:00, then yellow to 18:00.

z-track-south.text: IPMA's communiqué no. 3 (12:16): the low split into two centres and weakened. Our meteorologist's hypothesis (12:24): the centre over or just south of Lisbon about 13:00 to 15:00.

z-airport.text: Evidence (the press, citing ANA's site; not read at ANA): 222 cancelled by 09:20 (208 Lisbon, 14 Faro); 288 by 11:49; 334 by 12:35.

z-trains-bridges.text: Lusoponte's notice: since 11:30, 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril and 80 km/h on the Vasco da Gama. Fertagus normal; CP suppressed four trains over the bridge (12:00 to 15:00).

z-madeira-rain.text: IPMA's Areeiro station: 249.5 mm in six hours; 474.7 mm in twelve.

record_note: What the authorities had said, by our record, at the minute the questions were asked (13:09 UTC).
